call_input.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Create exactly ONE independent finished flat poster, portrait aspect ratio 2:3. This is a title-only Korean night-garden poster. Show the artwork itself edge to edge, with no mockup, wall, frame, panels or contact sheet.
요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Visual idea: a night garden becomes visible through differences in botanical density and the absence of darkness. A single continuous flat botanical field extends across the entire poster; several large bloom-shaped openings in that dark field reveal the pale ground beneath. The first glance should discover broad pale flower openings against dense darkness, then read the title held by the same figure-ground logic, then follow stems and paired leaves connecting the garden. This must be unmistakably growing flowers and foliage, never random speckling, stars, a generic ornamental texture, or a perspective view of a garden.

Composition and forms: a graphic relief-print-like arrangement seen as one flat plane, no horizon or vanishing point. Deep midnight indigo is the dense field. Botanical shapes are specifically branching, tapering stems with attached pointed leaves and open five-lobed night flowers. Two or three generous pale flower openings carry the image, varied in scale and naturally attached to stems; one broad opening approaches the upper-left region and another occupies the lower-right, with smaller partial blooms cropped intentionally at the edges. Allow dark leaf masses to alternate with pale leaf-shaped apertures, so positive and negative plant shapes can both be recognized. The stems must visibly connect leaves and flowers; do not scatter isolated petals. Concentrate the dark botanical density toward the edges and let irregular openings breathe inward, while preserving continuous growth above and below the title. Use a restrained second dark blue-green ink only to separate overlapping dark leaves, with no simulated 3D lighting. Crisp intentional contours with very mild relief-print edge character; predominantly clean solid ink surfaces, no blanket grain.

Typography and spatial relation: set the complete title on ONE horizontal baseline near the middle of the poster, spanning about four-fifths of the width. Use sturdy, carefully drawn Korean sans-serif forms with substantial even strokes, open counters and accurate syllable construction; warm pale ground-colored lettering. Keep two clear, normal word spaces, noticeably wider than the letter gaps. Let the botanical boundary form an irregular close clearing around the three word groups, with branching leaves approaching the outside edges of that clearing but never touching, crossing, filling or eroding the letter strokes or counters. This is not a separate banner or rectangular text box. The title is part of the field's pale openings, carrying the same positive-negative logic as the flowers. Maintain balanced outer margins so all letters are fully inside the canvas.

Text (verbatim, print exactly once): "밤에 피는 정원"

Only those six Korean syllables and the two supplied word spaces may appear as text. No quote marks, translation, additional words, subtitles, captions, dates, numbers, logos, symbols, decorative marks, borders or watermark. Preserve the exact spelling and visible word grouping. The entire poster should feel like a garden made legible by density and absence at night; no moon, stars, glow, gradient vignette, neon, metallic finish or photographic depth.

residuals: Flower apertures read more strongly as positive pale floral silhouettes than absence in darkness.
The protected title clearing reads as a largely horizontal lane instead of closely following three word groups.
Mottled dark print texture and a few merged leaf/stem junctions remain.
